court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: II Additional Subordinate Judge, Tiruchirappalli in A.S.No.103 of 2013
case_name: A.Gandhimathi vs Kamu Ammal on 8 December, 2023
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: A.Gandhimathi as plaintiff filed suit seeking declaration of title and injunction against Kamu Ammal from interfering with possession and enjoyment of suit properties. Appellant claims she was treated like a daughter by deceased couple, performed funeral ceremonies using her own money, and has a will executed in her favour. Defendant claims to be second wife of deceased Kamatchi Kunguli.

legal_principles.principle: Whenever there exists any suspicion as to the execution of the Will, it is the responsibility of the propounder to remove all legitimate suspicions before it can be accepted as the testator's last Will.
legal_principles.held: the initial onus on the propounder becomes heavier
cited_cases: Meena Pradhan & Ors. vs. Kamla Pradhar & Another, (2014)

legal_principles.principle: One who alleges fraud, fabrication, undue influence etcetera has to prove the same.
cited_cases: Meena Pradhan & Ors. vs. Kamla Pradhar & Another, (2014)

outcome.final_order: The judgment of the trial court is set aside and the original decree passed by the I Additional District Munsif Court, Tiruchirappalli in O.S.No.1275 of 2007 is restored.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
